title: Understanding Trap Seals in Drainage Systems
description: Every fixture connected to a drainage system relies on a properly maintained trap to prevent sewer gases from entering living spaces. The fundamental principle behind this defense is the water seal held within the curved section of the trap. If a fixture goes unused for a long period, evaporation can cause this water barrier to dry out, allowing unpleasant and hazardous gases to escape into the building. Professional maintenance involves recognizing signs of dry traps and understanding how proper venting prevents the siphon effect from pulling the water seal away during heavy fixture discharges.

Understanding Trap Seals in Drainage Systems

Every fixture connected to a drainage system relies on a properly maintained trap to prevent sewer gases from entering living spaces. The fundamental principle behind this defense is the water seal held within the curved section of the trap. If a fixture goes unused for a long period, evaporation can cause this water barrier to dry out, allowing unpleasant and hazardous gases to escape into the building. Professional maintenance involves recognizing signs of dry traps and understanding how proper venting prevents the siphon effect from pulling the water seal away during heavy fixture discharges.
